learned_action_value_estimate_comparison.methodology_note: Descriptive comparison of learned state-action value estimates only. In this empirical simulator, analytical ground-truth V*(s) is unknown; hence this difference reflects empirical divergence in action-value magnitudes rather than a direct measurement of true maximization bias. While Double Q-Learning decouples selection from evaluation to mitigate maximization bias theoretically, it is not strictly unbiased in practice.

scientific_verdict: In this discrete tabular 600-state environment, Double Q-Learning and Single Q-Learning achieve comparable asymptotic performance (p > 0.05). Double Q-Learning yields lower empirical variance across seeds and systematically lower learned action-value magnitudes, consistent with theoretical mitigation of maximization bias, though policy-level reward differences on this discrete task are statistically indistinguishable.
